scope: One bounded official-GitHub public-source audit of immutable-release repository-resurrection protection as a direct anti-ABA witness for stale generation publication. Tested documented tag non-reuse after immutable-release deletion, repository delete/recreate same-name protection, enable/disable semantics, rename/transfer scope, lightweight queryability, and zero-quota/zero-cost acceptance.

sources.observation: GitHub states that a published immutable release locks its associated tag to a commit; while the release exists the tag cannot be changed or deleted. If the immutable release is deleted, the tag may be deleted but the same tag name cannot be reused. GitHub also explicitly states repository-resurrection protection: deleting a repository and creating a new repository with the same name does not permit reuse of tags that were associated with immutable releases in the original repository.

GitHub documents repository- and organization-level enablement and says immutability applies only to future releases. The retrieved page does not establish a historical-reservation query API or the plan/quota eligibility needed by this Phase-1 acceptance gate.

GitHub documents authenticated REST endpoints to enable and disable immutable releases. The disable endpoint description does not state that disabling revokes the already-published immutable release tag-name non-reuse/resurrection protection; therefore that weakening path remains undocumented rather than assumed safe or unsafe.

GitHub documents transfer/rename behavior and a separate conditional permanent retirement of an OWNER/REPOSITORY-NAME combination for certain transferred repositories with Marketplace/action-use conditions. This is not documented as the namespace/lifetime rule for immutable-release historical tag reservations and therefore cannot fill that proof gap.

GitHub documents public listing of published releases, but the retrieved documentation does not establish a repository-independent or post-deletion endpoint that enumerates historical immutable-release reserved tag names after the release or repository is gone.

bounded_tests.evidence: associated Git tag is locked to its commit and cannot be changed or deleted while release exists

bounded_tests.case: immutable release deleted, old tag then deleted
bounded_tests.evidence: same tag name cannot be reused

bounded_tests.case: repository deleted then recreated with same name
bounded_tests.evidence: tags associated with immutable releases in the original repository cannot be reused
retrieved immutable-release documentation does not define historical tag-reservation namespace across rename

bounded_tests.evidence: transfer documentation's conditional OWNER/REPOSITORY-NAME retirement rule is separate and does not define immutable-release tag-reservation continuity
disable endpoint exists, but retrieved docs do not state whether already-published historical tag non-reuse/resurrection reservations can be weakened

bounded_tests.case: lightweight Chat-exposed query for historical reserved tag after release/repository deletion
bounded_tests.evidence: no stable repository-independent tombstone/reservation listing endpoint was established by the bounded official-source search

bounded_tests.case: zero monthly/trial/paid quota and zero paid-plan dependency
bounded_tests.evidence: retrieved official sources establish mechanism semantics but not the exact plan/quota availability needed for Phase-1 acceptance

observation_vs_inference.observation: GitHub provides a server-enforced anti-reuse rule for immutable-release tag names, including same-name repository resurrection, and retains tag-name non-reuse after deleting the immutable release.
observation_vs_inference.inference: This is stronger than ordinary repository-local CAS against one narrow ABA path, but it is not yet a complete direct anti-ABA witness for the recurring-Chat coordination protocol because namespace continuity, weakening controls, queryability after deletion, and zero-quota/plan scope are not fully documented.
observation_vs_inference.scope_guard: Do not generalize same-name repository resurrection protection to owner transfer, rename, arbitrary owner/name reuse, indefinite lifetime, or a queryable permanent tombstone without explicit evidence.

phase1_result.new_positive: Server-side immutable-release protection explicitly survives deletion of the immutable release's tag-name reuse opportunity and same-name repository resurrection, closing a narrower anti-ABA subcase without an external coordinator.
phase1_result.new_falsification: The available official documentation does not prove a stable queryable reservation namespace across rename/transfer/owner-name reuse, does not prove whether disabling immutability can weaken historical reservations, and does not prove zero-paid-plan/zero-finite-quota availability. Therefore the mechanism cannot yet serve as the accepted authoritative generation fence.
phase1_result.minimal_unresolved_child: Determine whether the historical immutable-release tag reservation is directly observable through a lightweight REST/ref creation failure or status surface after release/repository deletion, and whether that observable semantics is documented across rename/transfer plus zero-paid-plan/zero-finite-quota operation.

zero_dependency_zero_quota_assessment.reason: No quota-bearing compute was used or proposed, but exact GitHub feature plan/quota availability was not established by this bounded slice, so acceptance fails closed.

conflict_check: Only own LATEST state and official GitHub public documentation were used after semantic freeze. No O, other worker, downstream, legacy, shared-ledger, other-role receipt/config, or unrelated commit semantic input was consumed.
continuation: Part112: execute one bounded official-GitHub documentation leaf on observability of immutable-release historical tag reservations through lightweight Git/ref/release APIs. Specifically test whether creating a ref/tag whose name is reserved by a deleted immutable release has documented stable rejection semantics, whether any GET/status endpoint exposes the reservation after the release or repository is deleted/recreated, whether the behavior is specified across rename/transfer/owner-name reuse, and whether feature availability is documented for GitHub Free with no finite monthly/trial/paid quota. If any of those proof obligations remains undocumented, fail closed and persist the next candidate without executing a second leaf in the same invocation.
